 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY  Date : 21/04/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present Petition has been preferred by the Petitioner (Original Accused No.5) under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for quashing of the FIR being I - CR No. 24 of 2014 registered with Katargam R/CR.MA/3885/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 Police Station,
Jagdish Ramjibhai Ramoliya vs State Of Gujarat on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171442554/
1 Surat City for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 2. Heard learned Advocate Shri N.K.Majmudar for the Petitioner.
He submitted that in the present matter the dispute between the parties is of purely civil nature which is sought to be given a criminal colour by filing the present FIR.
He submitted that the present Petitioner has not played any role in connection with the offence in question.

The Petitioner has been roped in the present offence simply because the Original Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3, who happened to be the original owners of the land,
have executed a Power of Attorney for disposal of the land in question.
He therefore submitted that none of the ingredients for any of the offence alleged against the present Petitioner are made out from the averments made in the FIR.
He therefore submitted to allow the present Petition and quash and set aside the above referred FIR as regards the present petitioner.
3. The Petition is opposed by the learned APP Ms. Krina Calla.

She submitted that the land bearing Revenue Survey No. 191/1 situated at village Katargam Surat belonged to the Accused Nos. 1, 2, 3 and they had agreed to sell the said land in favour of the first informant.

The first informant had also paid the amount of consideration and, despite the same, Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3 were trying to dispose of the said land and, had executed a Power of Attorney R/CR.MA/3885/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 in favour of the present Applicant.
Learned APP submitted that the averments made in the FIR clearly indicate the culpable mind on part of the present Petitioner.
She therefore submitted to dismiss the present Application.
4. Though served, nobody appears for Respondent No.2.

5. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.
6.
At the outset it is required to be noted that the Hon'ble Apex court in its recent judgment in case of Usha Chakraborty v. State of West Bengal reported in 2023(1) Crimes 308 has held

entities.text: Usha Chakraborty v. State of West Bengal reported in 2023(1) Crimes 308
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the discretion under Section 482 of Cr. P. C. is to be exercised with care and caution and sparingly.

Exercise of said power must be for securing the ends of justice and only in cases where refusal to exercise that power may result in the abuse of process of law.
7.
The present FIR has been lodged by present Respondent No. 2.
It is contended in the FIR that the above parcel of land was owned by Accused Nos. 1,2,3 namely Ratilal Chhotubhai Patel, Rakeshbhai Ratilal Patel and Jayeshbhai Ratilal Patel.

The first informant and the aforesaid accused persons had entered into an agreement to sell and, qua the said agreement, the first informant had agreed to purchase the said land from the aforesaid accused persons for consideration of Rs.2,98,500/- and the amount of Rs.11000/- was R/CR.MA/3885/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 also paid in this regard towards the token amount in the year 1997.
Thereupon, the aforesaid accused persons had executed an irrevocable Power of Attorney in favour of the partner of the first informant namely Manubhai Ranchodbhai Patel.

Thereafter the first informant had paid the entire amount of consideration to the aforesaid accused persons and, pursuant thereto, the Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3 had executed a possession deed in favour of the first informant and, since then, the first informant was in possession of the disputed land.

On 6.5.1998 the first informant obtained the development Jagdish Ramjibhai Ramoliya vs State Of Gujarat on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171442554/
2 permission for developing the disputed land, since the first informant was desirous of selling out the disputed land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He did not insist for execution of sale deed in his favour from Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3.
However, such sale of land did not materialize, and therefore, on 27.1.2005, Accused No. 1, 2 and 3 had executed a registered sale deed in favour of the first informant.

After the sale deed was registered in favour of the first informant, Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3 executed a Power of Attorney in favour of the present Applicant authorizing him to sale the parcel of land to Accused No.4 namely Shailesh Nathabhai Ukani.

Accordingly, on 21.4.2005, the present Applicant executed a registered sale deed for the same parcel of land in favour of Accused No.4 Shailesh Nathabhai Ukani on the basis of the said Power of Attorney.

It is contended in the FIR that the present Applicant was aware about the fact that the parcel of land was already sold to the first informant and the registered sale deed in that regard had already been executed.
R/CR.MA/3885/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 8.

Considering the fact that the present Applicant was aware about the fact that the parcel of land,
for disposal of which, a Power of Attorney was executed in his favour, was already sold of to the first informant by Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3 and, even then, the present Applicant went on to execute a registered sale deed for the very same land in favour of another person, primafacie indicates the involvement of the applicant in the offence.
It is also required to be noted that the first informant had already paid full consideration to Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3, and thereafter only, a registered sale deed was executed in his favour.

9. It is sought to be contended on behalf of the Petitioner that the dispute between the parties is purely of civil nature and there are civil suits going on between the parties in this regard, and therefore, the present FIR is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
10.

It is required to be noted that when Accused Nos. 1, 2 and 3 were trying to dispose of the disputed land to some other person, it came to the knowledge of the first informant, and therefore,
he had filed Regular Civil Suit No. 908 of 2005 before the learned Civil Court at Surat, wherein, an interim injunction was granted in favour of the first informant, and despite the said injunction being granted, the accused persons including the present Applicant have disposed of the disputed land.
R/CR.MA/3885/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 11.
Considering these aspects, no case is made out for exercise of power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and hence, the present Application is hereby dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
Ad interim relief granted earlier stands vacated.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) J.N.W / 35 Jagdish Ramjibhai Ramoliya vs State Of Gujarat on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171442554/
